card.title: I Know Your Tells
card.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You chose the chipped mug. Bad news, isn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You held it through the whole story about losing our deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll use a glass. Can we just have tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only change cups when I've guessed. I'll sit down for this one.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 diagnoses bad news from mug choice, A3 cites a remembered loss, and A5 reads changing cups as confirmation that A has guessed correctly.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers an ordinary preference and B4 changes the vessel to get on with tea.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's attempt to remove the cue as another familiar cue, preparing to hear a serious disclosure.
